dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: sarvaṃ jagat svadehaṃ vā svānandabharitaṃ smaret | yugapat svāmṛtenaiva parānandamayo bhavet ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
sanskrit_variants: verse 65: Singh reports Lakshmanjoo's reading of vā as ca ('and': the world and the body together) rather than 'or'.
dharana.rendering: Let one call to mind the whole world, or one's own body, as filled with one's own bliss, all at once; through that inner nectar one becomes full of supreme bliss.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: 'all at once' means with the totality of attention in one sweep; 'one's own bliss' is the bliss of consciousness, not pleasure from objects; 'nectar' signals that it does not change. Kṣemarāja cites the verse on Śivasūtra 1.18 and 3.39. Singh reports Lakshmanjoo's reading of vā as 'and': the world and the body together.
dharana.technique_name: Body and World Filled with One's Own Bliss
dharana.instruction: Let a quiet, inner gladness fill your whole body, then the world around you.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 65 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: both filled with one's own quiet joy
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is the body, or the body and the world, filled evenly with a quiet, inner gladness.
geometry.svg_hint: a body outline glowing softly, the glow continuing outward into a wide circle
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Fill with gladness
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: a flat or ordinary mood is filled through with a quiet, self-sourced gladness. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Let gladness fill the body, then the world, at once
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The body, or body and world, felt as filled with one's own quiet joy
attention.secondary: That joy as inner, not dependent on anything outside

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Let one call to mind the whole world, or one's own body, as filled with one's own bliss, all at once; through that inner nectar one becomes full of supreme bliss.
adiyogi.method_summary: Recall a simple, quiet gladness that does not depend on anything outside. Let it fill the whole body at once, then the world around. Rest in that fullness without chasing intensity.

honesty.disclosure: Door 042 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 42 (verse 65) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 042 is dharana 42, verse 65. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. If no gladness is available today, that is fine; rest with whatever is present without forcing a feeling. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
